_: Per-app rule weightings. One review harness, three different problems --
reso-landing-app is a purchased marketing template and is largely an
aesthetics problem; reso-management-app is a design system and is mostly a
conformance problem, where the deterministic layer does nearly all the work;
A weight changes ORDER and SEVERITY. It never changes what is DETECTED. Every
rule runs on every app and every finding is written to the plan whatever its
weight, so the false-positive budget is invariant across profiles -- which is
the property fp_budget.py asserts rather than assumes. A profile that could
suppress a finding would be a way to make an app look clean by editing a JSON
file, and that is the failure mode this file must not have.
`never_below_1` is the hard floor: accessibility (A) and correctness (O) can
be weighted UP by a profile and never down. Marketing aesthetics is a reason
to care more about hierarchy, never a reason to care less about a 2.5:1
contrast ratio or a 30px touch target.

reso-management-app.rationale: Next 16 / React 19 / Tailwind 4 + Panda. A design system: conformance is the job, and the deterministic layer does nearly all of it.
notes: K is the highest weight in the fleet because a token violation here is
unambiguously a defect: there is a declared system and the element left it.
Gestalt stays ON but low -- a dashboard's hierarchy still has to work, and
the blind pass is the only thing that ever finds a defect nobody encoded.
It is the cheapest insurance in the pipeline and turning it off is how a
conformance-only review reports a clean page that reads as noise.
OPEN, and it is a K-family blocker rather than a weighting question: the
spec measured 0 `@theme` blocks in this app's shell CSS, so its Tailwind 4
engine emits utilities from no declared token source and every
Tailwind-authored colour is unattributable to a token by construction.
Where that holds, the K family owes INDETERMINATE (reason
`engine-has-no-token-source`), not FAIL and not a silent pass -- an
abstention routes to the vision layer, a pass routes nowhere. Encoding it
needs a per-app token map that only the surface stage can produce, against
the bytes in node_modules rather than a range in package.json.

reso-landing-app.rationale: Next 14, purchased template. Marketing aesthetics: whether it lands, not whether it conforms.
notes: K is weighted almost out because token drift against a purchased template
is measuring the template's own vocabulary and calling it a defect. The
findings are still emitted -- they are just not what a reviewer should read
first, and a page of them is how an automated reviewer loses credibility
before it says anything useful.
X goes UP: this is the app whose value is carried by hero imagery and
gradients, which is exactly where computed styles stop being able to answer
and the cross-check starts. Gestalt is the highest weight in the fleet for
the same reason -- 'does this land' is the actual question and no rule
reaches it.
A and O are floored at 1.0 by never_below_1 and are not negotiable here:
a marketing page is the surface most likely to be read by someone who has
never seen the product, on a phone, in daylight.

reso-web-app.rationale: Next 13. Between the two: product surfaces with a partial system.
notes: Deliberately flat. This app has not been profiled against its own routes,
and a made-up weighting reads as a measurement. Flat is the honest default
until the surface stage has run here.

bench-corpus.rationale: The ground-truth corpus. Flat, because a weighting would grade the instrument on a curve.
notes: Never weight the corpus. Scores measured here are what the rules do, and
a profile applied to the instrument would make every downstream number a
statement about the profile instead.
